transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, what brings me in is that my body just feels... completely out of my control lately. A little while ago, I was pacing around my apartment all night, just constantly moving, writing down all these notes for a supper club I wanted to start. I couldn't stop moving. But now... now I'm just so slowed down. My sister told me yesterday that it takes me forever just to put my shoes on. It's like I'm moving through mud.
During that time when you were pacing all night and couldn't stop planning the supper club, how many days in a row did that heightened, energetic state last?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, it's hard to keep track of time when you're going like that. It felt like a while, but I couldn't give you an exact number of days.
During that time when you were pacing and planning all night, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual, or feel rested even after very little sleep?

I'm not really sure. I mean... I was definitely awake all night, but I didn't really notice if I felt rested or anything like that. I just... I wasn't sleeping because I was so focused on getting all my ideas down. I don't really remember feeling like I needed less sleep, I just wasn't doing it.
Right now, while you're feeling so slowed down physically, are your thoughts still racing or do you still feel restless or keyed up inside, or does everything feel slow both physically and mentally?

Everything just feels... slow. Like, my brain feels just as heavy as my body does right now. I don't feel keyed up or restless at all anymore. It's just... quiet and sluggish, I guess. I'm not having any racing thoughts or anything like that. It's just a struggle to think or do much of anything.
During this slowed-down, heavy period, have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or that life isn't worth living?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean... I don't want to hurt myself or anything. It's not that I think life isn't worth living, it's just... I'm just so tired. I don't really have the energy to think about much of anything at all right now, let alone doing something like that.
Right now, how much is this slowed-down, heavy feeling affecting your ability to do daily things like getting dressed, eating, or going to work?

It's affecting everything a lot, honestly. I haven't been able to hold together my work schedule at the restaurant, or figure out my rent, or keep up with any family commitments. It just... it all kind of fell apart. My sister actually had to take me to the crisis clinic because I just couldn't get my basic responsibilities organized on my own anymore. Doing even the small things is just too much right now.
How many days or weeks has this slowed-down, heavy feeling been going on so far?
It's been... about three months now. Yeah, this heavy, slowed-down part has just been dragging on for about three months.
During these past three months of feeling slowed down, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like cooking or spending time with family?

Yeah, I have. The stuff that usually keeps me steady... like cooking, taking food photos, music, playing pickup soccer, even volunteering... it all just feels flat now. Like, I know I used to care about all of that, but I just... I can't make myself feel it anymore.

During these past three months of feeling slowed down and heavy, have you experienced anything unusual like hearing voices, seeing things others don't, or having thoughts or beliefs that others tell you aren't true?

No, I haven't had anything like that happen. I haven't heard any voices or seen things, and I don't think I've had any weird thoughts... no one's mentioned anything like that to me, anyway. It's really just the heaviness and not wanting to do anything.

During that time when you were pacing and planning all night, did it cause serious problems—like trouble at work, conflicts with family, or needing anyone to step in—or did it not really disrupt your daily life?

Yeah, it... it definitely caused problems. I couldn't really hold anything together. Like, my work shifts, paying rent, stuff with my family... it all just sort of fell apart. I was so caught up in everything I was planning that I couldn't handle basic responsibilities. It got bad enough that my sister actually had to step in and take me to the crisis clinic. So, yeah, it disrupted pretty much everything.
